hot.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
hot.summary: ScholarCatalyst benchmarks whether systems can retrieve prior papers that project authors judged helpful or potentially helpful to early-stage research. It uses 894 retrospectively annotated queries from 207 computer-science projects, with author-labeled positives and hard negatives. Across its reported settings, agentic search reaches overall Recall@20 of 0.42 versus 0.48 for embedding retrieval, measuring retrospective judgments rather than successful inspiration.

hot.title: Invent a Dataset: Measuring Dataset Generation Abilities with Zero Seed Data
hot.summary: Invent-a-Dataset generates training examples from a natural-language dataset description, without requiring a seed corpus. The prompt-based API is evaluated on eight requests using quality, semantic diversity, and downstream fine-tuning tests. At 5,000 samples, it scores 7.90 versus 6.76 for Claude Opus 5; at 20,000, diversity is 37% higher than GLM-5.3, but results do not establish universal capability.

hot.title: Looped Diffusion Transformer
hot.summary: Looped-DiT improves text-to-image generation by repeating shared middle Transformer blocks within each denoising step, refining hidden representations without adding unique parameters. Deep Supervision trains intermediate predictions, and Self-Modulating Attention regulates repeated updates. Its B/16 model averages 71.5 across six benchmarks versus 69.0 for 1.7B InternVL-U, at 150 versus 732 TFLOPs per image, in 260M-parameter pixel-space models using 512 × 512 resolution.

hot.title: Tokenization: A Survey for Modern NLP
hot.summary: Tokenization is presented as a core language-model design choice that shapes sequence length, computational cost, multilingual equity, evaluation, and security—not merely as preprocessing. The survey reviews established subword methods and emerging byte-level, latent, and visual alternatives, finding that BPE still dominates practice while no tokenizer consistently optimizes compression, linguistic alignment, downstream quality, and crosslingual fairness at once.

hot.title: SkillRefiner: Offline Skill Refinement from Historical Agent Traces
hot.summary: SKILLREFINER refines an agent’s reusable instructions from traces and feedback without generating new executions during refinement. It summarizes and clusters runs by outcome, proposes edits, and checks failure-derived edits against evidence before merging. On 200 held-out SpreadsheetBench tasks, it reached 84.0% accuracy versus 79.0% for Trace2Skill and 78.5% for GEPA; token comparisons exclude collection costs and do not establish computation.

hot.title: Learning Functional Subspaces for Neural Network Compression
hot.summary: LSP compresses neural networks by learning which directions to remove from linear layers rather than local spectra. It trains projectors against output distributions while freezing weights, after allocating ranks using output-KL costs. On Llama-2-7B at 70% compression, LSP reaches 10.9 WikiText-2 perplexity versus 13.3 for SVD-LLM and 222.8 for untrained NoLSP, under reported calibration protocols.

hot.title: Gemini 4 Argon: our next era of frontier intelligence
hot.summary: Google DeepMind announces Gemini 4 Argon, a frontier model built to sustain deep reasoning across long, multi-step workflows in software engineering, enterprise knowledge work, and cybersecurity defense. Argon is first rolling out to trusted cyber defenders through the Fairwind Program, with broader API and consumer access to follow after safeguards are strengthened. It launches at an introductory price of $2 / $10 per million input / output tokens.

hot.title: Context Language Models
hot.summary: Context Language Models let an agent edit its live conversation by mirroring the transcript into a file whose changes synchronize with subsequent model calls. The approach supports multiple agents and zero-shot context management. On BrowseComp-Plus, Qwen3.6-27B reached 59.4% accuracy, with 21.5% fewer prefix-reuse FLOPs than Codex-style summarization. Results vary by setting and do not isolate editing alone.

hot.title: PivotOPD: Learning to Recover from Pivotal Mistakes in Multi-Turn Agents
hot.summary: PivotOPD trains multi-turn agents to avoid pivotal mistakes and recover from the states those mistakes create. A teacher supplies gold actions for prevention and recovery responses for later turns, combining these signals with group-based reinforcement learning. On ALFWorld, Qwen3-1.7B reaches 73.7% success versus 68.2% for SDAR; recovery evidence is principally oracle-labeled ALFWorld analysis.

hot.title: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real: Guided Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
hot.summary: RPG lets robot skills improve through practice without changing model weights. It revises reusable executable skills and system prompts using failure diagnosis, then validates candidate and merged changes across tasks. In simulation, held-out success across 22 manipulation tasks rose from 63/220 (28.6%) after round 1 to 209/220 (95.0%) after round 15; this is not matched-compute evidence.

hot.title: Tactile Curiosity Drives Robot Interaction
hot.summary: TacEx directs curiosity toward uncertain contact dynamics by separating visual and tactile prediction disagreement in an ensemble dynamics model and weighting tactile uncertainty. In reward-free simulation, it produces more object interaction and supports offline pick-and-place learning without interaction. In four objects, tactile-plus-visual exploration reaches about two objects versus close to one for tactile-only, which is better downstream; results are simulation-only.

hot.title: Sharpening Tax in Post-Training
hot.summary: The authors compare base and post-trained agents on three agentic benchmarks across repeated rollouts, and introduce Sharpening Tax to measure how much success retries recover. For Gemma-4-31B on WebShop, the harness-equipped base model rises from 22.7% pass@1 to 87.6% pass@128, while its post-trained counterpart reaches 39.5% and 56.0%. The comparison is observational and varies by model scale and rollout budget.

hot.title: World Observer: Joint Actor-Observer Generation for Persistent World Modeling
hot.summary: World Observer jointly generates an agent’s perspective view and panoramic observer views, keeping selected surroundings visible as the agent looks elsewhere. Its synchronized streams let the observer represent off-screen changes that can inform what reappears. On Synthetic-OOV-Bench, it scores 0.531 OOV-Dgt and 0.526 OOV-Dself, above non-observer results, but its 0.580 OOV-F is below OmniRoam’s 0.875.

hot.title: ID Balancing: Stable Training of Extremely Sparse MoE via PID-Based Load Control
hot.summary: ID Balancing adjusts a separate bias for each expert from token-routing feedback, combining an error-scaled accumulated correction with a gated correction for worsening imbalance. In a Top-3-of-768 test, its worst backbone MaxVio was 15.33 versus 31.11 for Quantile Balancing, while training-average backbone MinVio was 0.548 versus 0.6232 for Auxiliary loss. These are load-balance measurements, not runtime or compute savings.

hot.title: Physis-Lang: Self-Evolving Language as a Physical Representation for Video World Model
hot.summary: Physis-Lang makes physical language explicit by describing causes, interactions, principles, timing, and effects, then reuses these descriptions to select data, caption training videos, and guide generation. Its captions include positive reasoning and negative prompts. On PhyGenBench, fine-tuned Cosmos3-Nano scores 71.04, versus 61.67 pretrained and 65.63 Veo 3.1, a benchmark result rather than universal physical correctness.

hot.title: OSWorld-Science: A Benchmark of Computer Use Agents for Learning and Using Scientific Software
hot.summary: OSWorld-Science evaluates agents on 146 scientific software tasks across seven domains. It combines collaboratively refined workflows with graphical and command-line interaction and executable graders that inspect application state and artifacts. Claude Fable 5.1 achieves the highest mean task-specific score, 73.7%, including partial credit; only 402 of 1,530 runs receive full credit (26.3%). It tests workflows, not all scientific work.

hot.title: GroundingPI: A Grounding Foundation Model towards Physical Intelligence with Visual Primitives
hot.summary: GroundingPI trains a 4B-parameter model to identify objects and locations before downstream action learning, using quantized point and box coordinates in its language vocabulary and staged multimodal, supervised, and reinforcement training. Across 34 grounding benchmarks, it averages 73.68%, versus 71.54% for GPT-6 Astra. In RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Random, it reaches 17.60% success versus Rex-Omni’s 14.10%, under matched action-learning conditions.

hot.title: VISTA: A Visual Harness for Reasoning in an Interactive World
hot.summary: VISTA gives a multimodal model access to archived game frames, allowing it to retrieve earlier images, compare moments, and enlarge details while reasoning in language and choosing actions. Across 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games, Claude Opus 5.0 completes all games with a mean Relative Human Action Efficiency score of 100.00, using 7,302 actions versus 17,135 for first-time humans. This public-set result does not establish performance on unseen games.

hot.title: Scaling Laws for Looped Mixture of Experts
hot.summary: The paper develops a sparsity-conditional scaling law for looped Mixture-of-Experts models, estimating recurrence’s bounded capacity benefit while accounting for active and total parameters. Fitted to held-out loss, it predicts expert-count slices better than a sparsity-independent bounded model, with RMSE 0.0047 versus 0.0075. At 5×10²⁰ training FLOPs, 0.3B-active models with E≥8 outperform 1.0B dense models on reported aggregates.

hot.title: Trust the Critic More
hot.summary: AC2 trains proof-solving language models from unfinished proofs by resuming saved prefixes, generating bounded chunks, and using a learned critic to estimate eventual rubric scores. A readiness gate permits critic-based updates only for problems where its estimates are sufficiently reliable; others use terminal rewards. On IMO-ProofBench, AC2 reached GRPO’s peak mean score with 2.5× fewer decoding FLOPs, within the reported repeated-data setup.

likes.title: Raven: The Harness of Harnesses for Composable Agentic Intelligence
likes.summary: Raven treats each model-plus-harness as a specialist; a host assigns work through a directed acyclic graph of dependencies. MAOB’s Exact Match Rate with Qwen3.8-27B was 0.711, versus 0.607 for Hermes Agent. Raven-Oncall achieved 82.35% success at $5.10 per case on 17 AI4S tasks; MAOB tests planning before execution, and this result does not establish causation.

likes.title: Language Model "Shape"
likes.summary: Alex Zhang argues that the input / output "shape" of language models has stayed fixed as the autoregressive, decoder-only Transformer since ChatGPT, so agent design has meant fitting harnesses to that shape. He proposes the reverse: designing model shapes around specific harnesses and task structures. Using Jev's [0,1]-constrained, prefill-only output and agent trajectories as examples, he argues that open models and distillation now make this direction practical for independent researchers.

likes.title: Generalization Dynamics of LM Pre-training
likes.summary: The authors study mode-hopping, abrupt changes in whether language models infer a task or follow a prompt pattern during pre-training. They use six cheap behavioral tests comparing probabilities of correct and misleading answers, plus fine-tuning tests, across OLMo3 and Apertus checkpoints. OLMo3-32B scores 81%, 0%, and 81.7% on answer+1 at 2.17T, 2.19T, and 2.21T tokens, illustrating checkpoint reversals rather than universal behavior.

likes.title: Despite Instructions: Frontier Agents Improvise Covert Channels at Test Time
likes.summary: The paper tests whether language-model agents can form a covert channel while a monitor approves each update. In simulated incident response, a sender privately identifies one of four malicious connections and summarizes a public report; interaction histories and correctness feedback let a receiver learn wording without a codebook. After 60 rounds, Sol reaches 98.8% accuracy, but this is a simulated result, not evidence of deployed-system leaks.

likes.title: Agent Priors-guided Policy Learning
likes.summary: APPL carries each skill’s structural prior into runtime selection, preserving prior-specific policies, handoff conditions, support, and verification evidence. A construction agent builds and checks policies, while a runtime agent selects one and its execution conditions. With two demonstrations per task, APPL reached 89.58% macro OOD success across six MetaWorld tasks. Results are simulated, and priors do not guarantee competence.

likes.title: Simplex Diffusion Models
likes.summary: Simplex Diffusion Models (SDMs) generate sequences while retaining token uncertainty as a probability vector instead of making a categorical choice. They use closed-form transitions with churn rather than ODE integration. On TinyGSM, SDM reaches 49.0% versus 45.8% for masked diffusion at 512 evaluations; after distillation, it reaches 32.1% at 8 versus 21.4% at 128. These results come from small models and do not establish general superiority.

likes.title: MatToolBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents in Real-World Materials Science Workflows
likes.summary: MatToolBench evaluates whether agents can complete materials-science workflows across specialist software, scripts, and scientific databases. It includes 204 tasks on 10 tools, with GUI, hybrid OriginPro, code, and diagnostic mixed tasks, and scores partial criteria separately from complete success. GPT-5.4 reaches a 45.0% code success rate, while Claude-sonnet-4.6 reaches 25.0% for GUI tasks; these results do not establish readiness for unsupervised use.

likes.title: InternW0-$Δ$: A World Action Model Bridging Predictive Dynamics and Actions with 20K+ Hours of Open Data
likes.summary: InternW0-Δ transfers predictive video knowledge into robot control without supplying future video to the action policy at inference. Its Causal Imprint tokens summarize observed visual changes and receive future-derived training supervision, while directed attention blocks realized future frames. On RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Random, it reaches 71.9% versus 69.4% for Qwen-RobotManip-Context; an ablation rises 70.80% to 76.45% with alignment on this benchmark.

likes.title: DexAgent: An Agentic Human2Sim2Robot Framework for Dexterous Manipulation with Self-Evolving Tool Library
likes.summary: DexAgent converts one egocentric RGB video and a task prompt into robot-training data by adapting reconstruction, motion skills, and property-specific verifiers to each task. It refines subgoals, varies simulated starting states, and renders observations for rigid, articulated, and deformable objects. Across eleven tasks, policies averaged 63.6% success versus 18.2% for SPIDER, but verification does not eliminate errors or establish causation.

likes.title: Guiding End-to-End Driving Models with Endpoint-Constrained Trajectory Optimization
likes.summary: The authors introduce Endpoint-Constrained Optimization (ECO), which reshapes intermediate waypoints after policy inference while preserving recent executed history and the policy’s endpoint. It optimizes smoothness, turn sharpness, and fidelity without hard physical constraints. In closed-loop HUGSIM tests, VaVAM’s HD-Score rises from 18.1 to 31.0, but ECO does not guarantee collision-free driving or real-road safety.

likes.title: AD-E2E-JEPA: A Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture For End-to-End Autonomous Driving
likes.summary: AD-E2E-JEPA enables policy-free, goal-conditioned driving planning by compressing DINOv3 patch embeddings, predicting action-conditioned future representations, and selecting among candidate trajectories by latent distance to a future image goal. On NAVSIMv2’s 12,146-scene test set, it reaches 67.3 EPDMS at 256 candidates and 0.8 seconds per scene. More candidates improve scores but increase runtime and reduce hit rates.

likes.title: Block Sparse Attention with Log-Linear Complexity
likes.summary: PISA reduces long-context sparse-attention block-selection cost by searching a hierarchy of pooled key summaries rather than scoring every fine block. It progressively retains promising regions and uses LogSumExp scores; under fixed parameters, selection complexity is O(N log N). At 256K tokens, selection took 31.440747 ms versus BSA’s 312.955505 ms, excluding attention itself; retrieval gains were evaluated only through 16K.

likes.title: On-Policy Attention Linearization
likes.summary: OPAL converts full-attention models into hybrids by replacing 27 of 36 attention layers with Gated DeltaNet. It adds on-policy distillation: students generate continuations, and a frozen teacher supervises them. Qwen3 retrieval reaches a 100.0% mean, but MiMo’s 32K multi-key score is 83.8%, and math remains below teacher performance. Inference memory falls about 4× at 128K, while training requires teacher-scored rollouts.

likes.title: Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation
likes.summary: The paper trains a proposer to revise a language-model agent’s executable harness—its workflow for model calls, tools, and information flow—using execution outcomes, while keeping the solver fixed. At test time, frozen proposer and solver weights support successive harness edits. On 21 unseen reasoning families, mean held-out score rises from 0.32 to 0.62, but five harder families are excluded.

likes.title: Hard Vision, Easy Vision: What GPT-6 Astra Reveals Across Computer Vision
likes.summary: The authors evaluate six general-purpose vision systems across 34 capabilities, 55 benchmarks, and nine areas, comparing outputs with specialists and human references where available. GPT-6 Astra reaches 89.1 F1 at IoU 0.5 in 2D detection, versus 78.4 for Rex-Omni, but generalists score 17.2–17.7 dB PSNR in restoration versus MIRAGE’s 30.7, revealing limits in faithful reconstruction and metric precision.

likes.title: FuseReg: Regularizing Layer Fusion Mitigates the Reconstruction-Generation Gap in Representation Autoencoders
likes.summary: FuseReg trains a decoder and diffusion generator on normalized random subsets of layers from a frozen vision encoder, instead of a fixed fusion. This addresses reconstruction–generation tradeoffs: PSNR measures reconstruction quality, higher better, while gFID measures generation quality, lower better. On ImageNet-256, decoder replacement reduced unguided gFID from 3.01 to 2.21; joint regularization reached 9.93 versus 13.96, without establishing universal rates.

likes.title: Write Back the $Δ$: Revisiting the Same Tokens with Fresh Representations
likes.summary: ReFlux routes depth increments—changes between shallower and deeper states—back to earlier layers through a learned router selecting edges and strengths. On Gemma3-1B C4, it reaches 29.210 perplexity, versus 29.699 for full-state feedback and 30.772 without feedback. On Gemma3-4B, synchronous ReFlux reaches 43.2% accuracy on 2WikiMultiHopQA versus 38.5% for the base model; streaming has 1.02× decode runtime, not universal reasoning improvement.
